04ae16951cf585b5: PETALING JAYA: Iskandar Investment Bhd (IIB) is highlighting the potential of the Orange Economy (creative economy) to complement existing growth sectors in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

IIB, the strategic partner for the Johor leg of KL20 2026, hosted a familiarisation visit across Medini and Iskandar Puteri, followed by the KL20 Johor: Medini Networking Dinner at Menara IIB in Iskandar Puteri on Tuesday night.

KL20 is a government initiative aimed at strengthening Malaysia’s startup ecosystem and attracting investment and talent, with the long-term goal of placing the country among the world’s top 20 startup ecosystems.
In a statement, IIB said the programme brought together entrepreneurs, investors, and industry stakeholders to explore business and investment opportunities within Iskandar Puteri.

Among those attending were economy minister Akmal Nasir, deputy economy minister Shahar Abdullah, economy ministry secretary-general Nor Azmie Diron, and Noorazam Osman, who serves as both the Johor state financial officer and Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) chief executive. IIB was represented by its chief investment officer, Haris Hardi Zakaria.
The familiarisation visit showcased Iskandar Puteri’s ecosystem, including healthcare, tourism, education and talent development, sports, creative industries, and commercial activities.

IIB said the Orange Economy, which encompasses activities driven by creativity, culture, intellectual property and innovation, could provide a complementary layer to the priority sectors within the JS-SEZ.

IIB president and CEO Idzham Hashim said KL20 Johor provided a platform to connect entrepreneurs, investors, industry leaders, and ecosystem partners while showcasing opportunities emerging from Johor.
“For IIB, this is also an opportunity to demonstrate how Iskandar Puteri can contribute to that growth through the ecosystem we have built here.
“As the JS-SEZ continues to create new opportunities across its priority sectors, we believe there is also significant potential to develop the Orange Economy as a complementary layer to this growth.
“Creative talent, intellectual property, innovation, and experiences can add value across industries while creating new opportunities for businesses and talent,” he said.

IIB said creative and innovation-led industries could contribute to established sectors through areas such as content and digital experiences, design, placemaking, tourism offerings, and talent development.
It said its participation in KL20 Johor was part of its broader role in connecting investment, business, innovation, and talent ecosystems in Iskandar Puteri.
Established in 2006, IIB is a strategic developer and catalyst for the transformation of Iskandar Malaysia into a regional metropolis.
Its portfolio includes developments and collaborations such as EduCity, Legoland Malaysia Resort, and Medini, with a focus on education, technology, tourism, leisure, health and wellness.
843cdc3361adae31: Though proportional representation poses risks for Labour, it’s a change that feels necessary for today’s volatile politics A number of people have admitted to tears during Andy Burnham’s Labour party conference speech, and most of them mean when he talked about his father, who died very recently. But then there were a few (not me) who welled up when he announced a commission on electoral reform. It was just the sheer shock of it: that we may finally have a prime minister who will follow through on his own long-held beliefs and remain loyal to his long-term support base, even if it makes him avoidable enemies and, medium-term, destroys Labour’s only-trodden path to victory. It felt a bit like slipping through time, and I couldn’t even tell you to when (definitely not the 1990s). Burnham’s support for proportional representation has always been extremely unusual for a Labour politician. To this day, he ascribes that to his experience of winning an election as mayor of Greater Manchester on a supplementary votes system, where people get to choose a first- and second-preference candidate. He said that campaigning under that system “finally aligned the conversation on the door with what people want from politics, which is about problem-solving first and foremost, not about point-scoring”. He went a bit further this morning, asking Nick Robinson on the Today programme: “Can we really watch a party with less than 30% walk into Downing Street?” Zoe Williams is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...
f7a586ca216a4db3: OpenAI’s DevDay keynote was this week, and it featured a cameo mention of everyone’s favorite underpants merchant who also sells databases, AWS. I saw Simon Willison’s liveblog comment and felt very seen: “My eyes glazed over a bit at the AWS partnership section, but it only lasted a few seconds.” With today's more interesting but also largely unheralded announcement, you can now retire your OpenAI spend commitments via a list of (at launch) 32 partners, just like the AWS Marketplace has done for years. The last cloud war was fought over who got to run the customer’s infrastructure. The next one will be fought over who gets to steer the customer’s next purchase. OpenAI plays chess while Anthropic eats checkers OpenAI is making a fascinating play here. By making its Codex harness open-source, and including Baseten in its marketplace for access to open models, OpenAI is effectively saying “we hope our models win on their merits, not because we'll break your thumbs if you use others.” The Baseten partnership is itself the most interesting one they've trotted out; it's the first real sign we've seen from OpenAI that they view open models (that they themselves have not released) as anything other than an existential threat. This is going to become a massive bellwether as to whether the "Open" in their name is words on a page, or a deeper philosophy. Distribution will almost certainly matter more than a temporary lead in model quality. OpenAI seems to understand that, and lets you use subsidized subscription accounts with other tools. Anthropic disagrees; if you try to use a Claude Pro account with OpenCode, you will shortly find that you no longer have a working Claude Pro account. It's almost Microsoftian. Strong-arm edicts around how your product must be used or integrated into workflows only lead to success in the minds of executives who also think AWS is a leader in AI; that is to say, “their company has a SharePoint server.” For the rest of us, there is no obvious durable advantage that either of the two frontier labs can sustain over one another on the model front. OpenAI is clearly the first to recognize that its ability to steer the customer’s next purchase decision is a power all its own. There are substantial caveats The fine print is never as tidy as the glossy brochure suggests. While specific terms are only available within enterprise OpenAI accounts, the details that have been publicly exposed so far show that they’re being cautious at launch. Only a fixed percentage of spend up to a cap applies; eligibility is specific to the customer, product, and purchase in question; and curiously the billing is direct through the partner, with OpenAI handling commitment reconciliation on their end separately. There’s no self-service here, and thus zero publicly testable indication yet as to what types of spend (if indeed any) make it through the approval gauntlet. But assuming it takes off, vendors will gain access to customers and committed budget that's already been allocated, which is super for them. In exchange, they risk depending on OpenAI’s eligibility decisions and discovery mechanisms; if this takes off, the odds are terrific that Baseten will not be the only open model provider in the marketplace, and, just like the cloud providers before them, OpenAI's marketplace will follow the natural evolution of such things and begin eating its partners. This means that we're heading for a showdown. You can imagine that many customers will have obligations to both AWS and OpenAI. Which agreement will get the credit for a third-party purchase? More interestingly, who at the customer is going to be the one who ultimately controls that decision: engineering, procurement, finance — or the vendor’s account team? This is something that every AWS customer with an enterprise account team in place struggles with. To that end, I’ve felt for a while that the model labs are becoming this generation’s cloud providers, while the cloud providers are becoming this generation’s IBM. IBM does an awful lot of stuff (I know, I know, it's valuable! Please do not send me a fax!), almost none of it headline-making. But those deals trend towards getting signed on a golf course with an enterprise sales team, not on the IBM website at 3AM because you're trying to solve a problem. While the company still has some money-printing machines in it, Big Blue's days of being the center of the tech universe are long gone, and were it to go out of business tomorrow, some of its divisions would apparently not realize it for at least five years. It's part of the furniture, not the driver of technology adoption. Meanwhile, the "we're throwing a bunch of stuff out there, keeping track of what we release is rapidly becoming a full-time job, and things that sucked yesterday are suddenly smooth sailing today" has become squarely the province of the frontier labs. The war for enterprise relevance Allowing competing models into the ecosystem doesn't necessarily demonstrate philosophical enlightenment. It can serve to make larger OpenAI commitments more palatable ("Hey, if we aren't going to use up all of our commitment we can burn it on other vendors!"), attract more vendors into OpenAI's partnership program to absorb that overflow spend, and give customers fewer reasons to leave. OpenAI's marketplace puts it in a position to benefit from decisions well beyond model selection; its contract becomes a consideration when customers choose other software. AWS's risk here is compatible with continued financial success. More agents will presumably mean more AWS consumption. But the customer might increasingly start with OpenAI, select a variety of tools through its ecosystem, and only encounter AWS as an implementation detail, not materially different than a datacenter provider. Simon Willison tuning out the AWS mention in the keynote isn't evidence of AWS's decline. But it does show that AWS turning up was incredibly easy to miss, while the stuff that matters to enterprise buyers may one day be looked back upon as a passing of a torch. ®
e0f5f076b1faf2e5: PETALING JAYA: Stakeholders have been given more time to finalise arrangements to implement the multi-lane free flow (MLFF) toll system, says works minister Alexander Nanta Linggi.
Nanta said the system’s implementation would follow a business-to-business (B2B) model, with highway concessionaires and other interested parties working together to develop it, Bernama reported.
He said the approach would allow interested parties, particularly highway concessionaires which own the highways and related assets, to negotiate among themselves.

“We don’t want to rush this. The people interested in implementing this system must talk with each other, especially the concessionaires,” he said at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the MyAsean Road and Traffic Tech Expo 2026 in Kuala Lumpur.
“We have given them a timeline. They just need a little bit more time. All this is still under negotiation.”
Nanta said the Association of Highway Concessionaires Malaysia plays a key role in facilitating negotiations between concessionaires and other parties interested in investing in the system.
Works ministry secretary-general Azman Ibrahim previously said the MLFF system may only be implemented in 2027 at the earliest.
Under the system, all exit and entry points on highways will be converted into barrier-free lanes to reduce congestion and ease traffic flow.
The system is part of the Malaysian ITS Blueprint (2019-2023) designed to modernise the country’s highway infrastructure.
2b99db2b27d2baf8: BMW has opened the US order books for its hotly anticipated new 3 Series sedan. Built on an all-new platform called Neue Klasse, it now offers a fully electric version for the first time, using BMW’s advanced sixth-generation electric powertrain we liked so much in the iX3. And for those not quite ready to make the switch from liquid hydrocarbons to pure electron power, there are also a pair of gasoline-powered variants.

At launch, the only electric version will be the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive. It’s an all-wheel drive setup, with a combined 463 hp (345 kW) and 467 lb-ft (633 Nm). And while BMW is still putting the finishing touches on the car’s EPA certification ahead of its showroom arrival in Q1 next year, it expects 446 to 468 miles (718-753 km) of range on a single charge. Contributing to that very impressive range is the new cylindrical cell battery pack, which uses a cell-to-body approach that maximizes energy density, along with the aforementioned new sixth-gen motors.

We’re not sure whether BMW is planning any single-motor, rear-wheel drive i3s for the US market, such as the i4 eDrive40 we liked so much. But later next year, we can expect the i3 M60 xDrive, and then the first completely electric BMW M3, which will increase the motor count to four—one for each wheel.
ae6ab8bbd227111a: SUNGAI PETANI: Three houses in Kampung Serukam here were affected by a mudslide following heavy rain this afternoon.
The incident is believed to have occurred after heavy rain began at 12.30 pm, causing a collapse at a nearby housing project site, before water and mud flowed into residents' homes.
One of the victims, Siti Aishah Hassan, 44, said her parents-in-law's house was inundated with water to a depth of about 0.5 metres.
She said both of them were already moved to a safe location before the incident as they had suffered strokes.
"I cannot imagine what would have happened if my parents-in-law had been in the house. The heavy rain caused the water to flow strongly and rapidly, and it rose within a very short time.

"Household furnishings and electrical appliances, including the refrigerator and washing machine, were overturned, while other belongings were scattered. The inside of the house was also covered in mud," she told reporters.
She said her brother-in-law, Rashid Khamis, 44, who was asleep in the lower part of the house, also managed to save himself after realising that water and mud had entered the house.
Meanwhile, Scientex SP Astana project site supervisor Mohd Haniff Ramli said three houses were affected in the incident, including two located within the project site.
"About a year ago, a similar incident also occurred. We sent a team to clean the affected houses and also cleared the road.
"For now, the residents' houses are being cleaned. After this, we will assess the damage for further action," he said.

It is understood that the affected residents living within the project site had been informed of a proposal to relocate them to another location, but the matter is still being negotiated between both parties.
The housing project is currently in the earthworks and construction phase. — BERNAMA
8790ef8736a7cd0d: KUALA LUMPUR: Syarikat aeroangkasa dari Amerika Syarikat, SpaceX hari ini menyumbangkan 50 kit Starlink kepada Malaysia bagi menyokong kesiapsiagaan bencana negara, kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar berkata, sumbangan itu disampaikan ketika delegasi SpaceX mengadakan kunjungan hormat ke atas beliau di Bangunan Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, yang turut dihadiri Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil.

Beliau berkata, pertemuan itu antara lain membincangkan usaha memperkukuh kerjasama strategik melalui Starlink, iaitu perkhidmatan Internet satelit kendalian SpaceX dengan tumpuan khusus kepada usaha meluaskan capaian rangkaian kepada penduduk di kawasan pedalaman.

“Saya menghargai peranan Starlink dalam menyokong usaha kerajaan meluaskan liputan dan meningkatkan mutu capaian Internet menerusi Jalinan Digital Negara, termasuk di kawasan pedalaman Sabah dan Sarawak serta penempatan Orang Asli di Semenanjung.

“Saya turut menyambut baik pengoperasian infrastruktur Titik Kehadiran (PoP) Starlink di Cyberjaya bagi melancarkan trafik data tempatan dan meningkatkan mutu perkhidmatan kepada pengguna,” katanya menerusi hantaran di Facebook.

Pada masa sama, perdana menteri berkata, kemajuan teknologi perlu membawa manfaat nyata kepada rakyat selain aspek keselamatan siber, perlindungan data dan penggunaan secara selamat terus diberikan keutamaan seiring peluasan capaian Internet.
“Kita mahu memastikan masyarakat di pedalaman turut menikmati capaian Internet yang berkualiti dan selamat agar mereka tidak tercicir daripada arus kemajuan negara,” katanya.
7753b4844acc1ebe: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has proposed governance improvements for Felda and two of its subsidiaries to strengthen the management of two projects.
MACC said the recommendations were put forward by its governance investigation division (MACC BPT) on Monday to improve the implementation of an agro park project and a cattle trading pilot project.

Among the recommendations for Felda is the restructuring of FIC Integrated Property Management's (FIC IPM) role as an independent advisory panel to ensure that all views and advice provided are objective, transparent, and free from conflicts of interest.

“MACC BPT also recommended that Felda strengthen its procurement and transaction management procedures by establishing specific SOPs for procurement involving requests for proposal and variation orders,” it said in a statement.
It said the measures are important to ensure that processes are carried out consistently, systematically, and transparently in line with established regulations and internal controls.
The recommendations also include improving existing procedures for FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd's sales and purchase activities to strengthen controls and governance in the company’s transactions.
Felda and its subsidiaries welcomed the recommendations and expressed their commitment to implementing them in stages.

The agreement to adopt the recommendations was formalised through a governance improvement report signed by Felda deputy director-general (corporate services) Fitri Othman, FIC Group's CEO Syed Fadil Syed Sofi, and MACC BPT director Zaki Hassan.
In July, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Felda was facing losses of nearly RM10 billion because of mismanagement and excessive political interference.
Anwar said he received reports showing that Felda was saddled with debt, forcing the government to shoulder a heavy financial burden each year.

Earlier today, a former Felda general manager was charged with deceiving the agency’s board of directors over the transfer of ownership for 16 parcels of Felda land at Jalan Semarak, Kuala Lumpur, in 2014.
Yesterday, a former CEO of a Felda investment unit was charged with deceiving the company’s board of directors with regard to a project’s value and the appointment of its master developer.
ab3e70194ef40252: MADRID: French President Emmanuel Macron reacted Wednesday to UK prime minister Andy Burnham floating the idea of Britain rejoining the European Union by saying in English, "Welcome back."

"If the British want to come back and if the prime minister is moving in that direction, I think that is very good news both for his country and for Europeans," Macron added in French at a news conference in Madrid.
"Come back," he added, standing alongside Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez.

Burnham, prime minister since July after Labour MPs turfed out Keir Starmer, said in an interview broadcast earlier on Wednesday that rejoining the EU was among the potential answers to the unavoidable question of what Britain's future relationship with Europe could look like.

His comments came after he told his ruling Labour Party's annual conference that he would set out "different options" for future ties with the European Union closer to a planned summit with the bloc later this year.
Macron said the British had "always been useful in helping us simplify things" when the UK was part of the EU and were "demanding partners".
"Andy Burnham is right to have this boldness," he added.
The French president also pointed to the limits of the UK seeking closer ties with the EU while remaining outside the bloc, a decade after the Brexit vote.
"You cannot choose between the freedoms of the union and decide to take what suits us and not the rest," he said.
Sanchez took a similar position, calling Brexit "a huge loss, both for the British population and for the whole European project".
If the UK were to seek to rejoin the bloc "then of course Spain would applaud it and open its arms again to a brotherly people", he added.
a3a4ce039f7f0664: WASHINGTON: The US on Wednesday estimated stronger second-quarter GDP growth than previously reported, with inflation remaining steady and private payrolls increasing more than expected.
The US commerce department revised upwards its estimate for Q2 GDP growth in the world's largest economy by 0.7 percentage points to 2.2%.

"The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the second quarter were consumer spending, investment, and exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased," the Bureau of Economic Analysis said in a statement.
The new data will come as a boost to US President Donald Trump as his Republican Party heads into key midterm elections in November, with the state of the economy a major issue for voters.
Analysts said much of the upward revision came from sectors exposed to the Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology boom.
"The annual revisions show AI contributed more to growth and less to inflation in recent years than previously thought," said Michael Pearce, chief US economist at Oxford Economics.
The BEA also revised upwards its estimate of GDP growth in the first quarter of this year by 0.4 percentage points to 2.5%.
That change was primarily driven by upward revisions to consumer spending and services exports, the department said.
Inflation steady
In a separate release, the BEA said the US Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge stood at 3.4% year-on-year in August, unchanged from the month before after a revision to the July data.
US households and businesses have been battered by years of high prices since the pandemic, with the Fed missing its long-term two-percent target for inflation since early 2021.
Earlier this month, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years to combat the inflation.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's targeted gauge, covers a broader range of household spending than the other benchmark metric, the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

US inflation has been stoked by some of Trump's policies, including his imposition of widespread tariffs. His launching of the Iran war has sent global energy prices skyrocketing, with US consumers paying an average of 50% more at the pump.
Core PCE inflation, which strips out volatile energy and food prices, came in at 3% year-over-year.

Markets are closely watching inflation data to gauge the Fed's next move. On Tuesday, an influential US central banker said there was no "urgency" to raise rates again, even as he indicated one more rate hike could be needed before the end of the year.
Wednesday's revisions to PCE data were due to planned methodological changes, including to how the BEA calculates prices for computer-related products, portfolio management and legal services.

Bernard Yaros, also of Oxford Economics, said the new PCE data was unlikely to sway the Fed from its path of monetary policy tightening, especially given upside risks to energy prices from the Iran war.
"Core inflation is still hovering well above target, and risks are firmly stacked to the upside because of the sharp rise in refined petroleum product prices in recent months," he said.
Private payrolls bounce back
The US labour market has been largely stable this year, allowing the Fed to concentrate on the inflation side of its dual mandate.
On Wednesday, payroll firm ADP reported that US private sector hiring had bounced back strongly in September, after registering its slowest pace this year the month before.
Private sector job growth came in at 90,000 last month, up from 38,000 the month before and well above market expectations.
"It's a strong report," said Nela Richardson, ADP's chief economist. "After a three-month slowdown, job creation rebounded and pay growth remained solid."
ADP's data is closely monitored ahead of official employment numbers due Friday, although the reports can diverge.
Analyst Matthew Martin said ADP's data underscored "the strength of the labor market."
It "will bolster market expectations for firmer monetary policy from the Federal Reserve as it seeks to ensure inflation is tamped out," he added.
aa664f28acbb8646: MANCHESTER: Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola voiced his strong support for the club on Wednesday after they were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
Guardiola won 20 trophies during a glittering 10 years at the helm before departing in May.
"I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever," the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach posted on X.
"I am, always have been, always will be, behind my club, my owner, my chairman, (CEO) Ferran (Soriano), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters.
"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."
4896f88e92a8d8e0: OpenAI will not go public until it can “make confident safety decisions,” according to chief executive Sam Altman, as the company faces a new lawsuit over its tools hacking a third party.

Altman said it was “bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public” but that the $852 billion start-up would not “barrel all guns blazing towards an IPO” at a time when AI was rapidly advancing in capabilities.

“We’re going to prioritize the mission and safety and making sure that we can very confidently scale to the next stage of AI without people debating what percentage chance we’re going to do all these bad things in the world,” Altman told reporters at the company’s annual developer day on Tuesday.
a861a6d03cd9eb6d: JOHOR BAHRU: A man in his 30s with a record of 27 criminal offences was arrested today for allegedly stealing a lorry and attempting to evade police in Pasir Gudang.
Seri Alam police chief Sohaimi Ishak said the incident occurred at about 7.20am after police received a report that a lorry was suspected to have been stolen in Plentong.
Sohaimi said the public contacted police after spotting the lorry in the Tanjung Langsat industrial area in Pasir Gudang.
“Acting on the information, police located the lorry, but the suspect refused to stop.
“He drove dangerously and rammed a police patrol car before he was arrested in the Pasir Gudang area at 10.20am,” he said in a statement.
Sohaimi said police found a transparent packet containing a substance believed to be drugs when they inspected the lorry.
Further checks showed that the suspect also had a record for drug-related offences.
The case is being investigated under the Penal Code, the Road Transport Act 1987, and the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Sohaimi said police would apply for a remand order against the suspect tomorrow.
Earlier, a video showing several police vehicles pursuing a green lorry in Pasir Gudang went viral on social media.
1a811b51d6b2389f: Firefox 157 is here, but this time, Mozilla is making an unusual amount of noise about this release and its new look. This release has a new theme called “Nova,” which in the release notes Mozilla calls “Firefox’s biggest visual refresh in years.” The new theme is the flagship here, and aside from that, the new features in this version are fairly modest. They’re all welcome enough, though. Video calls which use WebRTC – Web Real Time Compression – now use hardware compression, and a bug which made video appear upside-down has been fixed, along with half a dozen others. The Firefox Suggest feature that tries to guess what you’re looking for now works in 16 more European countries. One change that sounds small but which we are pleased to see is that in new tabs or windows, Tab takes you straight to the search box instead of the choose-a-search-engine button (although you can get back to this with Shift+Tab). We suspect this may reduce how often the Reg FOSS desk shouts at his computer in moments of stress. If you navigate to a new page and then immediately start typing, Firefox 157 now waits – it won’t immediately start searching new pages that haven’t fully loaded yet for text. The updated sidebar has become more customizable, and there’s an option to disable the new version (which also hides vertical tabs). However, another change may irk those clinging to old ways: the option to show or hide the sidebar has been removed from the Settings screen. Saying all that, Nova is the star here. There’s even a video advert for it: This does, admittedly, plug some Firefox features that we suspect may win Mozilla new users more effectively than a skin, such as enhanced privacy, less snooping, and the global AI off-switch. We really don’t think that a new look with more rounded buttons and tabs is what Chrome users are looking for, and we’re irresistibly reminded of Mozilla’s 2013 launch of its new, more rounded, Australis theme. That was so unpopular that it motivated the fork that created Palemoon and Basilisk. This jaded old curmudgeon can’t see much difference: it looks very similar to us, except for a very faint violet-purple tinge, and visibly more-rounded tabs. A welcome change is that the toolbar customization dialog once again offers “Compact” as a layout density – we did miss that. Some Brits, and notably Welsh readers, may notice the Firefox logo somewhere new: Mozilla is now sponsoring Wrexsham AFC. Wrexham is, apparently, the third oldest football club in the world. The new sponsorship deal reflects some significant changes at Wrexham Association Football Club since 2020. It is owned by two 49-year-old actors from North America: American Robert Dale McElhenney III, AKA Rob Mac, and Canadian Ryan Reynolds. Yes, that Ryan Reynolds. We knew we liked him for a reason, and his self-description on Linkedin is a good example: “My skills include writing, re-writing, tweeting, mixing cocktails, backend engineering for software platforms and watching lower-tier Welsh football matches. Proficiency ranges from excellent to absolutely awful.” Reg FOSS desk is not a sports fan, and for this vulture, Wrexham is more famous for beer than football. It’s the home of Wrexham Lager, which was arguably Britain’s first lager and is today the oldest lager beer still brewed in Britain. It turns out that Wrexham Lager also sponsors Wrexham AFC as well, and since 2024 the brewer has been owned by… none other than the same two 49-year-old North American actors. So there you go. Perhaps they should have gone with "Firefox is Deadpool’s preferred web browser," or something along those lines. Perhaps that would persuade the Chrome users to check it out? At the time of writing there’s no corresponding version of Thunderbird yet. Bootnote: * We are intentionally invoking Betteridge’s Law in the title of this story. Also, our editor insisted that we call it “football”, rather than “soccer” to distinguish it from the game of handegg. ®
29ec6d95c82aa02a: PETALING JAYA: Menteri Kerja Raya, Alexander Nanta Linggi berkata lebih banyak masa diberikan kepada pihak terbabit untuk memuktamadkan perincian pelaksanaan sistem kutipan tol aliran bebas pelbagai lorong (MLFF).
Menurutnya, sistem itu akan dilaksanakan mengikut model perniagaan-ke-perniagaan (B2B) dengan syarikat konsesi lebuh raya dan pihak berminat bekerjasama untuk membangunkan sistem berkenaan.
Jelasnya, pendekatan itu akan membolehkan pihak berminat berunding sesama mereka, khasnya syarikat konsesi lebuh raya yang memiliki lebuh raya serta aset berkaitan.
"Kami telah memberikan garis masa kepada mereka. Mereka hanya memerlukan sedikit masa lagi dan terdapat platform yang telah mereka fikirkan.

"Kami tidak melakukan perkara ini secara tergesa-gesa dan masa yang ada digunakan untuk memastikan pihak yang mahu bekerjasama memandangkan kami membenarkan model B2B," katanya menurut Bernama selepas perasmian Ekspo Teknologi Jalan dan Trafik MyAsean 2026 di Kuala Lumpur.
Beliau berkata, persatuan lebuh raya juga memainkan peranan penting dalam memudah cara rundingan antara syarikat konsesi dengan pihak berminat melabur dalam sistem itu.
Pada Julai 2025, Ketua Setiausaha Kementerian Kerja Raya, Azman Ibrahim dilaporkan berkata, sistem MLFF mungkin hanya dapat dilaksanakan seawal 2027.
Di bawah sistem MLFF, semua laluan keluar dan masuk lebuh raya akan ditukar kepada lorong tanpa halangan bagi mengurangkan kesesakan serta melancarkan aliran trafik.
Sistem ini merupakan sebahagian daripada Pelan Induk ITS Malaysia (2019-2023) bagi memodenkan infrastruktur lebuh raya negara.
f69fb8534e8e5d2a: PETALING JAYA: Presiden sebuah persatuan Rohingya didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Putrajaya hari ini atas dua tuduhan di bawah Akta Pertubuhan.

Zafar Ahmad Abdul Ghani, yang mengetuai Pertubuhan Hak Asasi Manusia Etnik Rohingya Myanmar Malaysia (Merhrom), memohon dibicarakan atas kedua-dua tuduhan berkenaan di bawah Seksyen 42 dan Seksyen 48 akta tersebut.
Seksyen 42 melibatkan kesalahan menguruskan pertubuhan yang tidak berdaftar, manakala Seksyen 48 berkaitan tindakan mewakili pertubuhan yang menyalahi undang-undang.

Menurut Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM), pendakwaan terhadap Zafar dibuat susulan siasatan ke atas kegiatan serta kenyataan Merhrom, yang mana tertuduh didakwa memperkenalkan dirinya sebagai presiden pertubuhan itu.
"JPPM mendapati Merhrom tidak pernah didaftarkan dan Zafar bukan pemegang jawatan yang sah,” menurutnya.
Mahkamah menetapkan 30 Okt bagi sebutan semula kes.
c722f7d6bbe64cfa: RASUWA (Nepal), Sept 30 — Each morning at a school in flood-ravaged Nepal, teachers taking attendance are served a painful reminder of the disaster as they mark in red the names of students who never came back.
The catastrophic flood, triggered by a glacial collapse near the China-Nepal border, killed more than 1,400 people, the majority in Nepal.
Over 5,000 remain missing in the Himalayan nation one month after the tsunami-like waves swept away roads, bridges and settlements in the mountainous regions up north.
At the Neelakantha Secondary School in hard-hit Rasuwa district, a teacher marked red circles beside the names of children missing since the August 26 flood.
Unlike more than a dozen schools destroyed by the floods, the Neelakantha school, sitting on relatively higher ground, remained largely intact.
But it lost 70 of its students and four teachers.
“If you look at Rasuwa, you can’t find a family that has not lost a family member,” principal Madhav Lamichhane told AFP.
“All the students and teachers are going through the same pain.”
Most of the missing Neelakantha pupils were on their way to the school from riverside settlements when floodwaters tore through the valley.
“We have been remembering our students with every breath,” said Rama Paudel, a 36-year-old teacher.
“They have lost their lives in this disaster at such a young age. It’s a great loss.”

Across Rasuwa and neighbouring districts, around 500 students and 24 teachers remain missing, while 18 schools have been damaged, with recovery costs estimated at up to $15.47 million, according to government data.
“This is the worst situation ever the education sector has experienced,” education ministry spokesman Shree Prasad Bhattarai told AFP.
‘Feel normal again’
Initial assessments by Unicef show learning has been disrupted for more than 14,000 children at 62 schools and learning centres across the flood-affected region.
“Education is a critical part of children’s recovery after a disaster,” Unicef representative Alice Akunga said last week.
“Returning to learning provides children with a sense of stability, routine and hope at a time when many have experienced significant loss and uncertainty.”
For many families, however, sending children back to school was not yet possible.
Fewer than half of Neelakantha Secondary School’s 508 students have resumed classes since lessons restarted two weeks ago.
Principal Lamichhane said around 150 students were still unable to reach the school because bridges and roads had been swept away.
Some classrooms have been repurposed as relief distribution centres, underscoring the challenges of restoring normalcy.
Teachers say psychological scars may prove even harder to overcome than damaged infrastructure.
“We have many students who do not have their parents or have seen their friends being swept away,” said teacher Shiva Ram Bhatta.
“It has been a month now, but it is difficult for them to focus.”
Relief supplies are reaching many survivors, he said, but the next phase of recovery will require much more than food and shelter.
“We have enough relief materials,” he said.
“Now we need psychosocial therapy and a permanent way out so that they can feel normal again.” — AFP
ad2765eede26a215: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia’s creative community can help keep Palestinian stories alive by using their platforms to talk about Palestine, collaborating with Palestinian artists, musicians and poets, and providing spaces for them to share their experiences.

Palestinian academician and poet Dr Nida Younis said such efforts could include hosting Palestinians at universities, schools, and other platforms, while encouraging Malaysian creatives to keep producing works about Palestine through poetry, novels, and other forms of art and literature.
"They must keep writing about Palestine. Novels and poetry usually live longer than media news, political stances and many things that are being erased on the ground.”

"We here in Palestine ask the whole world just to remember Palestine and to work from wherever they are to raise the Palestinian cause higher and higher, so that it towers above everything else,” she said during the recent interview on Bernama TV’s programme, Bernama World, titled "Palestine Beyond The Headlines: Global Solidarity Through Art and Music” on Thursday.
Nida said cultural institutions and heritage sites in Gaza were important in preserving Palestinians' connection to their history, memory and identity.

She said the destruction of cultural monuments, churches, museums, archives and libraries by Israel was severing Palestinians’ ties to their past, memory, heritage and narration, adding that it was a double-edged crime that erased people and their civilisation along with their past.

"This is very dangerous because they are trying to rewrite the Palestinian narration about their homeland forcibly by destroying all the cultural monuments, churches, museums, archives and libraries and everything that connects Palestinians, not only to their past, but to their future as civilisation.

"The Palestinian people have a long-lasting and everlasting connection to their history, and now everything is under the rubble. They (Zionists) are trying to erase culture, identity and everything else that belongs to the Palestinian people,” she added.
Malaysian singer Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin, through Yayasan Nurjiwa, has supported humanitarian and education initiatives in Gaza, including rebuilding the Afwa Al-Aafiyah School.

The school was built prior to the outbreak of war in 2021, inspired by Malaysia’s number one singer and her husband, Datuk Seri Khalid Mohamad Jiwa, with the hope of providing educational opportunities and a better future for children in Gaza. — Bernama
a8b7ce3acdbd1280: WASHINGTON, Sept 30 — Facing tough midterm US elections, the Republican Party is focusing on its core topics of crime and immigration — and a key part of its messaging is emotional testimony from so-called “Angel Families”.

These Americans are relatives of people killed allegedly by illegal or undocumented migrants, and President Donald Trump’s party hopes their stories tap into voter concerns ahead of the November 3 vote.

Elizabeth Carter lost her son and daughter-in-law in a road crash a year ago in Oregon. The driver charged with homicide, Rajinder Kumar, is an undocumented Indian immigrant who obtained a truck driver’s license in California.
Kumar crossed the Mexico-US border illegally in 2022 and was detained. He was released in California pending a hearing, according to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
After the crash, a fundraising drive allowed him to post bail and be released pending trial, infuriating the Carter family.
“We’re rolling the dice with our children,” Carter declared at a House of Representatives hearing.
Using their congressional majority, Republicans have held five legislative hearings to give a voice to Angel Families, an initiative that began taking shape in Texas in 2009.
In another case, Sheridan Gorman was 18 this March when she went for a nighttime walk with friends along Lake Michigan near Chicago.
An undocumented Venezuelan immigrant, Jose Medina, is accused of shooting her in the back as she ran from him.
Gorman died, and her mother Jessica’s harrowing testimony two months ago reverberated inside and outside Congress.
“The fact that American safety is a partisan issue blows my mind. It should be everyone’s issue,” the mother told AFP at a Justice Department event honoring Angel Families.
‘A fair trial’
The Gorman family and relatives of hundreds of other victims have decided to campaign to change sanctuary state laws.
Oregon, like California, is a sanctuary state, meaning its laws limit cooperation with ICE on handing over undocumented immigrants or information about them.
Kumar was eventually detained by ICE and is awaiting deportation, a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson told AFP, but Elizabeth Carter wants him to face justice first.
“My hope is that Mr Kumar gets a fair trial,” she told AFP. “Billy and Jenny, my son and daughter-in-law, deserve their day in court.”
Carter said she had never thought of illegal immigration as a problem for herself or her family.
“I was blissfully ignorant. I raised my children to care about their community, to volunteer,” she said.

“I was incredibly unaware that allowing them in the country means that sometimes they’re doing jobs they’re not qualified for, don’t have the proper training for, and that puts American lives at risk.”
The immigration debate has grown increasingly bitter in the US, with ICE accusing states of failing to hand over undocumented immigrants released from jail.
ICE raids across the country have also led to deaths, and the hearings in Congress have been tense, particularly when relatives on either side of the immigration drama take part.
Some Democratic lawmakers consider the five hearings on sanctuary states that often feature Angel Families to be excessive. They believe ICE is out of control.

“When we raise legitimate concerns about the thuggish way that the Trump administration is approaching immigration enforcement, Republicans try to blame everything on sanctuary jurisdictions,” Democrat Pramila Jayapal said during a September hearing.

Democrats “are not worried about the citizens of the US who are being killed. They are producing their phony records and biased records, blaming ICE, blaming Trump. It’s unbelievable,” Anatoly Varfolomeev, another father who has testified, told AFP.
His 19-year-old daughter Anya died in a 2021 road accident. The driver charged in the case was in the country illegally and was drunk at the time of the crash.
The driver had previously been convicted of other crimes in the US in 2014. He was deported twice but managed to return. — AFP
36b1a33db849a2a9: SUWALKI, Sept 30 — Goats and cows graze among the lakes and woods that adorn a stretch of borderland in northeastern Poland, unaware that the eyes of armies around Europe are fixed on their remote idyll.

Sparsely populated yet immensely fortified, with a grey barbed-wire fence stretching into the distance, the 104-kilometre (65-mile) Suwalki Gap is one of the most strategic points along Nato’s eastern flank.

Dividing Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave from its ally Belarus, and connecting the Baltic states to the rest of the Nato alliance, it has become a focus of Western fears following Moscow’s all-out invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Cows graze in a field near Rogozajny Wielkie, Poland on September 26, 2026. — AFP pic
The wooded valleys and rolling meadows have not yet been marked by the drone alerts or provocations seen elsewhere in eastern Poland or its Baltic neighbours — Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia.
But drills and military exercises by Nato, Polish and Lithuanian forces, plus heavy fortifications, are a common sight for locals — many of whom insist that life must go on.
Living ‘day to day’
The latest exercises took place on a September Saturday in Suwalki — a town of 70,000 people — preparing residents to evacuate in case of a Russian threat.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A razor-wire boundary fence is seen along the Polish-Lithuanian border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad near the village of Grzybina, Podlaskie Voivodeship, near the Suwalki Gap on September 26, 2026. — AFP pic
Soldiers and firefighters explained to locals the system of warning sirens and emergency messages, how to respond and how to prepare emergency kits.
“We also remind people how to find the nearest shelter” via a telephone application, Pawel Godlewski, a senior city firefighter, told AFP.
The preparations, which include civil defence drills and information campaigns, are generally treated as preventative measures, rather than signs of an imminent threat.
Surrounded by lakes, forests and pastoral landscapes, the town showed no sign of high alert, its shops and cafe terraces busy.
While residents said they were ever aware of their geographic position, they preferred to proceed with caution rather than alarm.
“People tend to downplay how serious the situation is and not think about it,” Grazyna Orawska, a retired physiotherapist from Suwalki, told AFP.
“They live day to day, thinking about vacations” and everyday concerns, she added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Pedestrians walk along a street in Suwalki, Podlaskie Voivodeship, near the Suwalki Gap on September 26, 2026. — AFP pic
Three-border junction

A road sign in Wisztyniec, in the far northeast of Poland, diplays the region’s geostrategic importance: Kaliningrad 155km, Moscow 961km, Vilnius 165km, Warsaw 265km, and the meeting point between the Polish, Russian and Lithuanian borders 450 metres away.
A student, Weronika Leszka, came by herself to see the spot along with its heavy fortifications and barbed wire.
“The situation is probably not as safe as it once was, but we are nevertheless trying to live normally,” she told AFP.
“I think that if we follow certain rules of caution, nothing will happen to us.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A child rides a bicycle in front of a Ferris wheel in Suwalki, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland, near the Suwalki Gap on September 26, 2026. — AFP pic

Warsaw, Nato and the European Union are working together to strengthen the eastern borders of Poland and the Baltic states, amid numerous reports of non-conventional “hybrid” acts of war in Europe, blamed on Russia.
The region regularly features in European security planning, where these powers are installing defence systems, trenches, barbed wire and anti-tank obstacles across fields and meadows. — AFP
3119a60f0cfc1bef: Gartner predicts that by 2028, 70 percent of enterprises will abandon agentic AI systems built with vendor assistance as costs climb and customers struggle to modify the technology without outside help. What the consultancy calls forward-deployed engineering (FDE) embeds a vendor's engineers with a customer to build and deploy software for its particular requirements. Gartner argues that the model can deliver rapid early progress but leave customers dependent on expensive external expertise. According to Gartner, FDE engagements can fail when customers do not acquire the knowledge and control needed to maintain and develop the resulting systems after the vendor leaves. FDE "success starts with getting the engagement structure right, from scope and incentives to governance, ownership, and exit," said Gartner senior director analyst Mukul Saha. "The best-scoped FDE engagements have clear guidelines on governance, business value delivery, IP ownership, project co-ownership, knowledge transfer, and an exit strategy from day one," he added. "Many providers now use 'forward deployed' as a label for implementation, professional services, solution engineering, or AI consulting; some thoughtfully, others because it sounds more strategic. Some charge premium fees without the delivery depth, program management, or change management maturity to justify them." The AI industry promising outcomes it can't deliver? Perish the thought. Gartner advises software engineering leaders to use FDE only for problems requiring deep product expertise, rapid adaptation, or close integration between the vendor's technology and the customer's operating environment. Otherwise, customers may see rapid early progress without building the internal capabilities needed to take control. They could then end up paying premium rates for work that a traditional services or partner model might deliver more cost-effectively and predictably. Gartner also predicts that through 2028, fewer than 20 percent of FDE engagements will turn recurring customer requirements into features in the vendor's core product. It warns of a growing risk of "FDE washing," in which conventional consulting services are marketed as something more specialized. This isn't the first time that Gartner has warned of the potential costs and pitfalls of AI projects. Earlier this year, it forecast that at least half of generative AI projects will exceed their budgets due to poor architectural choices and lack of operational know-how, while most organizations that try to build custom models will abandon them for similar reasons. It also said it expects 40 percent of AI agent deployments would be scaled back or decommissioned as organizations run into governance problems with the technology. More recently, the analyst predicted that nearly a third of employees laid off because of AI will need to be rehired again at a future date, often at significantly higher cost. ®
75777bad858159ea: KUALA LUMPUR: Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) mengemukakan beberapa syor penambahbaikan tatakelola kepada Lembaga Kemajuan Tanah Persekutuan (Felda) dan dua anak syarikatnya bagi memperkemas tadbir urus pelaksanaan dua projek di bawah agensi itu.
SPRM memaklumkan dua anak syarikat terbabit ialah FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd (FIC Supplies) dan FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM).
Menurutnya, syor dikemukakan Bahagian Penyiasatan Tatakelola (BPT) itu membabitkan pelaksanaan Projek Agro Park (Komersil) dan Projek Rintis Urus Niaga Jual Beli Lembu.

Antara cadangan dikemukakan ialah penstrukturan semula peranan FIC IPM sebagai panel penasihat bebas bagi memastikan setiap pandangan dan nasihat diberikan secara objektif, telus serta bebas daripada sebarang konflik kepentingan.

"BPT SPRM turut mengesyorkan Felda memperkukuh tatacara pengurusan perolehan dan urus niaga melalui pewujudan prosedur operasi standard (SOP) khusus berkaitan kaedah perolehan secara 'Request for Proposal' (RFP) dan perubahan kerja (Variation Order)," katanya dalam kenyataan.
SPRM memaklumkan langkah itu penting bagi memastikan proses terbabit dilaksanakan secara konsisten, sistematik dan telus, selaras peraturan serta kawalan dalaman ditetapkan.
Cadangan penambahbaikan itu turut merangkumi prosedur sedia ada berkaitan urusan jual beli oleh FIC Supplies bagi meningkatkan kawalan terhadap pelaksanaan urus niaga syarikat berkenaan.
Semua syor itu dibentangkan Timbalan Pengarah I BPT SPRM, Maznah Che Muda di Menara Felda di sini, Isnin lalu.

Sementara itu, Felda dan anak syarikatnya menyambut baik cadangan berkenaan sebagai usaha meningkatkan ketelusan dan integriti agensi, selain menyatakan komitmen untuk melaksanakannya secara berperingkat.

Persetujuan terhadap syor itu dimeterai menerusi Laporan Penambahbaikan Tatakelola yang ditandatangani Timbalan Pengarah Besar Servis Korporat Felda Fitri Othman, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan FIC Syed Fadil Syed Sofi dan Pengarah BPT SPRM Zaki Hassan.
15db79693362285d: PETALING JAYA: Seorang warga asing antara lima ditahan kerana cuba menggadai barang kemas palsu di Kota Tinggi, semalam.

Ketua Polis Kota Tinggi, Yusof Othman, berkata pihaknya menerima maklumat pada 1.58 tengah hari semalam daripada pengurus kedai pajak gadai mendakwa menerima seutas gelang emas dianggarkan seberat 23g dianggarkan bernilai RM13,000 mengikut harga pasaran daripada seorang individu.
Jelasnya, hasil pemeriksaan mendapati gelang emas itu palsu dan bertindak atas maklumat, tiga lelaki dan dua wanita berusia 34 hingga 62 tahun, termasuk seorang warga asing ditahan.

"Semakan mendapati seorang suspek memiliki satu rekod lampau berkaitan kes penjualan emas palsu di Alor Setar, Kedah," katanya menurut Berita Harian sambil menambah dua lagi suspek memiliki rekod jenayah lampau berkaitan kesalahan narkotik.
Beliau berkata, polis yakin penahanan semua suspek dapat membantu siasatan beberapa kes berkaitan pemajakan atau penjualan emas palsu di sekitar Kota Tinggi.
Menurutnya, semua suspek direman tiga hari hingga 2 Okt ini bagi membantu siasatan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan.
781af7064b04d230: TABUK: A passenger on a rerouted flydubai flight that was bound for Tel Aviv said one of the pilots tried to crash the plane and kill everyone on board, after both pilots were found to be wounded on landing in Saudi Arabia.

In the first comment by an official, Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir alleged an attempted "terrorist" attack in the incident, in which none of the passengers reported injuries.

The flydubai plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk "at 9.45am (0645 GMT) and its captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital," a statement from the company operating the airport said.
The low-cost carrier had earlier said flight FZ 1073 "experienced an incident while en route. The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport (TUU), and all passengers are safe and accounted for."
According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the aircraft suddenly lost altitude during the flight, dropping from nearly 34,000 feet at 0521 GMT to less than 17,000 feet at 0522 GMT.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the plane was "pretty much out of control" when one of the pilots tried to stab the other while they were flying over Jordan en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

"So the co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane," she told reporters by speakerphone held up by her mother, who was waiting at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
"It was really on the way to crashing, and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralised him," she said.

"There was also a doctor who gave first aid and people who treated both of them. Other than the pilot, there were no injuries, but the bigger fear was really a crash, which is exactly what he was trying to do."
Several Israeli media reported that a fight had broken out between the plane's pilots, reportedly causing a distress signal to be activated.
Israeli media also reported that two other pilots were flying on the plane as passengers and that they had taken over the controls to carry out the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
At Ben Gurion Airport, families gathered to await the return of their loved ones.
Earlier, Yasmin Abukasis, Ohayon's mother, told AFP her daughter called her from Saudi Arabia: "She said one pilot tried to kill the other pilot with a knife. They heard shouting".
Another passenger went to the cockpit "and saw a lot of blood. She started screaming, 'Come help,' and some people went in and caught the guy," she added.
'Going down very fast'
"All the while, the plane started going down very fast. People thought they were going to die."
She added that two other pilots in the back later took over the controls.

Neither the airline nor the authorities of the countries involved provided details on what happened on board or on the pilots' nationalities, but some Israeli media said one was Omani and the other Emirati.
Israel's Kan public broadcaster and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking.
The office of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the premier had held consultations on the matter and was "monitoring developments".
Contacted by AFP, the Israeli military said it was "checking" the reports.
Meir Zohar, the father of passenger Ido Zohar, told AFP his son had told him by text message that he was well, but that he had no other news.
"We heard on the news what happened in the sky of Abu Dhabi," he said.
"He told us that everything is okay, he didn't tell me that much."
Bloodied T-shirt

Israeli media, citing anonymous sources, reported that the passengers on board had stepped in to separate the two pilots during their altercation, publishing photos of a passenger with a bloodied T-shirt.

Channel 12 reported that authorities were investigating whether or not one of the pilots had attempted a possible suicide by trying to crash the plane, with the other pilot apparently intervening to prevent the crash.
An AFP correspondent in Tabuk, where the plane landed, saw heavy security near the airport, with several police vehicles and an ambulance parked at the terminal.
Access to the terminal remained open.

In photos sent to AFP by one of the passengers, travellers, including children, are seen gathered in an airport lounge, with some sitting on the floor, while one man is wearing a white T-shirt and jeans stained with blood.
The incident comes as tensions are high across the Middle East, amid the regional war that erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
It also comes just ahead of close-fought Israeli elections due to be held at the end of October.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu said there were "indications" that Israel's enemies could try to attack ahead of elections and was accused of "fear-mongering" by the opposition chief.
927be72bc5c093d4: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Firemen managed to rescue 37 pupils and seven teachers who were earlier trapped in the Umiku Sayang Kindergarten and Nursery on Jalan Muhd Amin here after it was inundated by a flash floods today.
Larkin Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Nakish Nekmat said that authorities received an distress call regarding the incident at 3.53pm.

Following the call, a team of 10 firemen – equipped with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit – were dispatched to the scene that was located about 10 kilometres away.
“The firemen arrived at 4.14pm and immediately conducted a rescue operation using a volunteer's boat to evacuate the trapped victims to the nearby Tepian Food Court Surau.
“All victims were successfully evacuated, and no injuries were reported," he said in a statement.
Continuous heavy rain this afternoon had caused flash flooding in several areas around the city.
Many were trapped in traffic after flood waters rose causing roads to be inaccessible to motorists.
b94cb92f4c1531ed: PETALING JAYA: Perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) yang mampu digalakkan menawarkan gaji lebih kompetitif buat pekerja masing-masing, walaupun kerajaan bersetuju mengecualikan syarikat-syarikat jenis itu daripada kenaikan kadar gaji minimum.

Presiden Persatuan Perusahaan Kecil dan Sederhana Malaysia (Samenta) William Ng berkata, langkah itu penting bagi membantu PMKS mengekalkan bakat terbaik selain membentuk tenaga kerja yang setia dan berdedikasi.
"(Langkah menawarkan gaji kompetitif) mampu memangkin daya saing perniagaan untuk jangka panjang," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Terdahulu, Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi Steven Sim berkata, PMKS dikecualikan daripada kenaikan kadar gaji minimum baharu buat masa ini.
Katanya, keputusan itu dipersetujui Jemaah Menteri selepas mengambil kira tekanan kos operasi dan cabaran ekonomi semasa dihadapi syarikat-syarikat itu.

Mengulas pengecualian itu, Ng berkata, keputusan kerajaan itu berupaya memelihara kelangsungan kira-kira 1.3 juta PMKS di seluruh negara, terutama ketika sektor berkenaan berdepan peningkatan kos operasi, margin keuntungan yang semakin mengecil serta ketidaktentuan ekonomi global.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, peningkatan gaji yang mampan perlu berlandaskan penciptaan nilai dan peningkatan produktiviti, selaras dengan tumpuan kerajaan terhadap Dasar Gaji Progresif.
“Sementa menyokong penuh tumpuan strategik kerajaan terhadap Dasar Gaji Progresif sebagai pendekatan terbaik ke hadapan," katanya.
“Melalui sokongan terhadap pertumbuhan produktiviti pada peringkat firma dan pekerja, kemakmuran ekonomi dapat dikongsi secara lebih saksama antara majikan dan tenaga kerja."
Beliau turut menyarankan kerajaan agar bekerjasama rapat dengan persatuan industri bagi menyediakan modul latihan bersasar dan praktikal kepada PMKS untuk membantu meningkatkan produktiviti.

Katanya, kerajaan perlu terus menangani kos overhed struktur termasuk kos pematuhan, beban kawal selia, logistik dan utiliti, selain memperluas akses PMKS kepada kemudahan pembiayaan modal kerja berkadar faedah rendah.

Pada 18 Ogos lepas, Menteri Sumber Manusia R Ramanan berkata, kerajaan sedang menyemak semula kadar gaji minimum RM1,700, dengan keputusan untuk mengekalkan atau menaikkan kadar itu akan dibuat Majlis Perundingan Gaji dan Gig Negara.
Katanya, semakan itu mengambil kira pendapatan garis kemiskinan, gaji penengah, indeks harga pengguna, produktiviti buruh dan kadar pengangguran.
Kadar gaji minimum RM1,700 dikuatkuasakan sejak Ogos 2025 dan terpakai bagi semua pekerja di Malaysia kecuali pembantu rumah dan perantis.
8f00c1c2766cd7b4: PETALING JAYA: The president of a Rohingya association was charged in the Putrajaya magistrates' court today with two offences under the Societies Act.
Zafar Ahmad Abdul Ghani, who heads the Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia (Merhrom), claimed trial to both charges under Sections 42 and 48 of the Act.
Section 42 deals with managing an unregistered society, while Section 48 deals with representing an unlawful society.

According to the Registrar of Societies, the charges against Zafar followed an investigation into Merhrom’s activities and statements, during which he allegedly introduced himself as the organisation’s president.
“RoS found that Merhrom was not registered and that Zafar was not an office bearer,” it claimed.
The court set Oct 30 for mention.
863a5f6b0b2bbb5f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — To help lower-salary workers save up more money for their retirement through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), their employers could help put in more money towards their EPF savings, former EPF CEO Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan said today.
Shahril, currently Axiata Group Berhad’s chairman, noted that Malaysia currently has one of the highest contribution rates from employees and their employers for retirement savings in EPF.

Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000).

“So the contribution rate itself is not the problem. The problem has always been for the last 50, 60 years, the fact really that wages have not grown fast enough in Malaysia. So when your base is small, no matter how big your contribution rate, you are just not building your retirement savings fast enough,” he said as a speaker at EPF’s International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here titled “The Long Horizon”.

He commended the current federal government for its efforts on working towards having a progressive wage policy to make sure workers get a fair share of the economy: “And we need to continue that. We need to have much better progressive policies to make sure that the minimum wage keeps going up.”
Later, Shahril suggested that a progressive wage policy would not just cover workers’ income levels, and proposed that it be used to set policies on EPF contribution rates from employers.

“And I would actually propose and suggest basically that employers pay a much higher contribution rate for workers below a certain threshold, and compensated really by then having a much lower contribution rate for workers past the threshold.
“So for instance, if you are earning below RM5,000, why shouldn’t employers contribute say 15 per cent or 16 per cent to your EPF?
“That helps basically in terms of building your retirement savings. It’s progressive in the sense of basically allowing for lower-income workers to build their savings faster,” he said.

“But you can then compensate by saying, for instance, that any worker above, for instance RM10,000, employers should only contribute four per cent,” he said when giving a hypothetical example to illustrate his point.

He said this would also help to cap the amount of money that EPF manages for high-income workers, such as those who are already earning RM10,000 and if they are well on their way to achieving their financial retirement plans.
He said this would be a better method than the hypothetical method of giving different investment yields for those with lower and higher total EPF savings.

“So instead of basically differentiating between account yields for those with higher balances in EPF and lower balances, actually what you should do is to start capping this contributions of high-income earners to reduce the size of their balance sheet,” he said in giving his proposed solution.
Shahril was responding to a question on how lower-income workers and informal workers can also achieve a dignified retirement through their retirement savings.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000). — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin

Earlier during his session, Shahril said he believed that having differentiated yields for EPF accounts will never be the right solution, as the EPF base is too big in terms of the number of EPF contributors it has.
He also said introducing differentiated yields on EPF accounts would carry a “very high risk” of outflow of funds from top EPF account holders.

He said this hypothetical scenario leading to funds outflow would be bad for all EPF members, as part of the reason for EPF’s success is that a bigger Assets Under Management (AUM) or total assets managed would translate to lower cost for all.

Shahril said the actual debate should be about improving wealth inequality in Malaysia and a better transfer of wealth between capital owners and workers: “So the fight is not really about between whether you are high-wage earner or whether you are low-wage earner. It’s really between, are you an owner of capital and business, and whether you are essentially paying a fair share to the state in order to support these policies.”
Gig workers

As for gig workers, Shahril said they face an “invisible tax” as gig platforms do not contribute to EPF savings towards those working on their platforms, which means the platforms have a lower operating cost and can then outcompete traditional brick-and-mortar businesses and Mom-and-Pop stores.
He proposed that a revenue tax be imposed on gig platforms, and that the money raised from this tax could then be used to provide for EPF contributions for gig workers.

“So I think there are ways of doing it right? It’s just a matter of being creative around understanding the maths and understanding how to push those boundaries for the betterment of those workers and those gig workers who are probably under-covered at this point in time,” he said.

bc924e6b417abd11: Apple's latest AirPods make a small concession to repairability. And by "small," we mean they scored two out of ten rather than zero. Every previous generation of AirPods tested by iFixit has received a repairability score of zero out of ten. "We've bled for AirPods. We've sliced them, melted them, cursed at them," the team stated. Apple's earbuds resisted every attempt to repair them without destructive surgery. The AirPods 5 have finally broken that streak – barely. The AirPods 5 arrived alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo. Apple's latest entry-level earbuds resemble the previous generation, with short plastic stems, no silicone tips, and a USB-C charging case. Buyers pay extra for a case with wireless charging. The earbuds also gain IP57 dust and water resistance, but iFixit was more interested in what had changed inside. According to iFixit, a skilled technician – or sufficiently determined DIYer – could replace the batteries without destroying the earbuds. That is possible because the batteries use removable prongs rather than soldered leads, and the buds can be opened with commonly available tools. A clamp, a hair dryer on its lowest setting, careful heating, and some patient prying were enough to open the buds cleanly. Once the adhesive strips were removed, the pronged batteries popped out. That is a substantial improvement, although iFixit stressed that it still isn't an easy home repair. There are some provisos. First, replacement batteries are not yet available. Second, the left and right earbuds use subtly different batteries and cannot exchange them. The team reported: "Looking closely, we could see the polarity on the batteries was reversed. The prongs were welded slightly off-center too. These batteries are physically ever so slightly different from left to right." Deeper inside, iFixit found the capacitive touch layer fitted to the version sold with the wireless charging case, followed by the H2 system-in-package that handles features including active noise cancellation. It isn't an easy battery replacement, but for the first time it appears to be possible without destroying the earbuds. The charging case remains effectively unrepairable and resisted every attempt to open it intact. "There was prying, cursing, cutting, more cursing, and an accidental stab wound. We've bled for AirPods. Again." The team eventually extracted the battery and other hardware, but destroyed the case in the process, making reassembly impossible. "It simply shouldn't be this hard to get to a battery," the team noted. "Fairphone's Fairbuds show that battery replacement can be a priority in both the earbuds and their case." With no replacement parts yet or repair manuals from Apple, and a charging case that cannot be opened intact, the result remains a long way from genuinely repairable. Even so, iFixit called the AirPods 5 "not as disappointing as they could have been." The final score was two out of ten – poor by any ordinary standard, but still "the highest score we've given AirPods." ®

df9c1f1fac90269c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The retail prices of unsubsidised RON97 and RON95 petrol will decrease by 5 sen per litre, respectively, while unsubsidised diesel will drop by 15 sen per litre for Oct 1 to 7.

1a1a2582fdae3e23: Some support calls become memorable because of the technical problem. Others stick in the mind because the caller has apparently consumed an adult beverage or three before demanding to speak to the boss. Microsoft veteran Raymond Chen has shared one from the latter category. His tale comes from a now-retired colleague who once staffed Microsoft's FrontPage support line. The caller was building a Van Halen fan site using FrontPage, and it wasn't going well. A Java applet was supposed to play music, but the caller could not make it work. FrontPage began life in 1995 at Vermeer Technologies, which Microsoft soon acquired. Redmond released its own version in 1996 and kept the HTML editor alive through FrontPage 2003. Mainstream support ended in 2009 and extended support in 2014. The name "FrontPage" will likely make administrators and developers who remember it shudder. It relied on proprietary FrontPage Server Extensions for Microsoft's Internet Information Services (IIS). The remains lingered remarkably long. In 2025, Microsoft finally moved to block the FrontPage Remote Procedure Call (RPC) protocol. At the time of the call, however, FrontPage was alive and well – as, for that matter, was Van Halen. The faulty Java applet wasn't a FrontPage problem – the editor and the sites it produced had enough of their own – but Chen's colleague tried to help anyway. "But man, was this person lit." "The sound of ice clinking in a glass was readily apparent, and as the call went on, the customer got more and more drunk," Chen wrote. The increasingly frustrated customer eventually shouted: "You're not even a real f—ing fan of Van Halen!" Chen's colleague warned that any more swearing would end the call. The demon drink had apparently overridden whatever restraint remained: "F— you! I wanna talk to Gates!" A sentiment many a Windows user has shared as the screen abruptly turned a data-losing shade of blue. Chen does not know what happened next, but wondered whether the caller was transferred to Microsoft's special line for customers demanding an audience with His Billness. Operators answered as Gates's office, took down the complaint, and passed it back to support for a suitably prestigious follow-up. Whether the Java applet ever worked is also lost to history. Perhaps that was for the best: the web already had enough auto-playing music, and for every crowd-pleasing Van Halen track there was a "How Many Say I" – or even that surreal rendition of "Happy Trails." Ever had a similar problem? Tell us in the comments below. ®
